$comment: The news module's register. news/tools/poll.py reads this file; news/AGENTS.md explains the fields. An id here is also the prefix of the source id a page cites.

feeds.note: The 'san-francisco' feed carries the whole Bay Area; the item's <category> tags are the real filter — one item is tagged San Jose, Oakland, Bay Area and San Francisco at once.
Mission-district focused, and the densest address source of the set: street numbers reach the headline often.

Openings and closings — address-rich, but the 'san-francisco' edition files stories from Guerneville, Oakland and the Peninsula under the same feed. Trailing slash matters: without it the request 301s.

NOT POLLED. rss.bizjournals.com/robots.txt ends with a blanket 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /' after the Cloudflare-managed group that allows it, and names ClaudeBot among the crawlers it disallows. research/AGENTS.md says a source that forbids automated access is a needs-human question, not a workaround. Left registered so the decision is visible; set access to 'open' to poll it.

Posts, not articles: no <title> at all, the headline has to come out of the post text, and the article URL is the last link in it — often a bit.ly. The account posts national and Hawaii weather stories too.

Same shape as the Chronicle account. Its links are sfexaminer.com articles with utm_ parameters — strip them before citing. Overlaps sf-examiner; the cursor pair keeps one article from being read twice.
Commercial real estate across Northern California — sales, leases and development, so a high address rate on the items that are actually in the city. Its <category> tags name the county or city.
Covers Oakland and the wider region under the same feed.
robots.txt allows '*' and blocks named AI crawlers (ClaudeBot, GPTBot). We poll the feed it publishes for readers, identify ourselves, and link back.
A section page, not a feed: no dates and no summaries, so the cursor is the set of article URLs seen. robots.txt allows '*' on /news/ and disallows named AI crawlers by name.
